label: John 20:1
text: Now on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene went early, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and saw the stone taken away from the tomb.

label: John 20:2
text: Therefore she ran and came to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and said to them, “They have taken away the Lord out of the tomb, and we don’t know where they have laid him!”

label: John 20:3
text: Therefore Peter and the other disciple went out, and they went toward the tomb.

label: John 20:4
text: They both ran together. The other disciple outran Peter, and came to the tomb first.

label: John 20:5
text: Stooping and looking in, he saw the linen cloths lying, yet he didn’t enter in.

label: John 20:6
text: Then Simon Peter came, following him, and entered into the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying,

label: John 20:7
text: and the cloth that had been on his head, not lying with the linen cloths, but rolled up in a place by itself.

label: John 20:8
text: So then the other disciple who came first to the tomb also entered in, and he saw and believed.

label: John 20:9
text: For as yet they didn’t know the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead.

label: John 20:10
text: So the disciples went away again to their own homes.

label: John 20:11
text: But Mary was standing outside at the tomb weeping. So, as she wept, she stooped and looked into the tomb,

label: John 20:12
text: and she saw two angels in white sitting, one at the head, and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.

label: John 20:13
text:
They told her, “Woman, why are you weeping?”
She said to them, “Because they have taken away my Lord, and I don’t know where they have laid him.”

label: John 20:14
text: When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing, and didn’t know that it was Jesus.

label: John 20:15
text:
Jesus said to her,
“Woman, why are you weeping? Who are you looking for?”
She, supposing him to be the gardener, said to him, “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away.”

label: John 20:16
text:
Jesus said to her,
“Mary.”
She turned and said to him, “Rabboni!” which is to say, “Teacher!”

label: John 20:17
text:
Jesus said to her,
“Don’t hold me, for I haven’t yet ascended to my Father; but go to my brothers, and tell them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’”

label: John 20:18
text: Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord, and that he had said these things to her.

label: John 20:19
text:
When therefore it was evening, on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were locked where the disciples were assembled, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the middle, and said to them,
“Peace be to you.”

label: John 20:20
text: When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side. The disciples therefore were glad when they saw the Lord.

label: John 20:21
text:
Jesus therefore said to them again,
“Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.”

variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of John': 'ο Ιησους (Jesus) omitted in א D L W Ψ 050 lat syr s co'. The World English Bible prints 'Jesus therefore said to them again'.

label: John 20:22
text:
When he had said this, he breathed on them, and said to them,
“Receive the Holy Spirit!

label: John 20:23
text: If you forgive anyone’s sins, they have been forgiven them. If you retain anyone’s sins, they have been retained.”

label: John 20:24
text: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, wasn’t with them when Jesus came.

label: John 20:25
text:
The other disciples therefore said to him, “We have seen the Lord!”
But he said to them, “Unless I see in his hands the print of the nails, put my finger into the print of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.”

label: John 20:26
text:
After eight days again his disciples were inside, and Thomas was with them. Jesus came, the doors being locked, and stood in the middle, and said,
“Peace be to you.”

label: John 20:27
text:
Then he said to Thomas,
“Reach here your finger, and see my hands. Reach here your hand, and put it into my side. Don’t be unbelieving, but believing.”

label: John 20:28
text: Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!”

label: John 20:29
text:
Jesus said to him,
“Because you have seen me,
you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen, and have believed.”

label: John 20:30
text: Therefore Jesus did many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book;

label: John 20:31
text: but these are written, that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in his name.

variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of John': ζωην αιωνιον ('life eternal') is read by א C(*) D L Ψ 0100 f13 33 it vg mss syr p,h cop sa,bo Irenaeus lat; ζωην ('life') by 'rell' (the remaining witnesses). The World English Bible prints 'life'.

label: Mary Magdalene went to the tomb alone while it was still dark
statement: On the first day of the week Mary Magdalene went early, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and saw the stone taken away from the tomb (20:1); she comes alone and in darkness, where the Synoptics name a group of women at dawn or sunrise.
note: John's difference from the Synoptic accounts: Matthew has Mary Magdalene 'and the other Mary', Mark three women 'at sunrise', Luke a larger group 'at early dawn'; John has Mary Magdalene alone 'while it was still dark'.

label: Mary ran and reported to Peter and the beloved disciple that the body had been taken away
statement: Mary ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, saying 'They have taken away the Lord out of the tomb, and we don't know where they have laid him' (20:2); the report presupposes a body removed, not a resurrection.

label: Peter and the beloved disciple ran to the tomb, and the beloved disciple arrived first
statement: Peter and the other disciple went out and ran toward the tomb; they both ran together and the other disciple outran Peter and came to the tomb first (20:3-4).
note: John's difference: Luke 24:12 has Peter alone running to the tomb; John pairs him with 'the other disciple whom Jesus loved', unnamed in the text.

label: The linen cloths lay in the tomb and the face cloth was rolled up in a place by itself
statement: The beloved disciple saw the linen cloths (othonia) lying without entering; Peter entered and saw the linen cloths lying and the cloth that had been on his head (soudarion) not lying with the linen cloths but rolled up in a place by itself (20:5-7).
note: John alone separates the face cloth from the linen cloths; Luke 24:12 knows only 'strips of linen lying by themselves'.

label: Mary saw two angels in white sitting in the tomb
statement: As Mary wept she stooped into the tomb and saw two angels in white sitting, one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain; they asked why she was weeping (20:11-13).
note: Miracle/reception claim, written and searched honestly; John's two seated angels differ from Matthew's one descending angel, Mark's one young man in a white robe and Luke's two men standing in dazzling clothing.

label: The tomb stood in a garden, and Mary supposed the man she met to be its gardener
statement: Mary turned and saw Jesus standing but did not know him; supposing him to be the gardener she asked him to say where he had laid the body so she could take it away (20:14-15); the exchange presupposes a burial garden kept by a gardener (19:41: 'in the place where he was crucified there was a garden; in the garden a new tomb').
note: The gardener is John's detail: no Synoptic account has Mary mistake the risen Jesus for the tomb's keeper.

label: Mary addressed the risen Jesus as 'Rabboni', glossed 'Teacher'
statement: Jesus said 'Mary'; she turned and said to him 'Rabboni!' - 'which is to say, Teacher' (20:16). Rabboni is the Aramaic honorific (literally 'my master/teacher'), one of the Greek Gospel's transliterated Aramaic terms with a gloss.
note: The first-century currency of the title is debated: the fetched Rabbi article records the Jewish tradition that 'rabbi' or 'rabban' was first used after 70 CE, so Gospel-era uses may be retroactive honorifics. John's own glossing habit parallels 1:38 ('Rabbi... being interpreted, Teacher').

label: On the evening of the first day of the week the risen Jesus stood among the disciples behind locked doors and showed his hands and side
statement: When it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, with the doors locked where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, Jesus came, stood in the middle, said 'Peace be to you', showed them his hands and his side, and the disciples were glad (20:19-20).
note: Appearance claim, written and searched honestly. John's difference from Luke 24:36-43: John's doors are locked for fear, Jesus shows hands and side; Luke has him invite touch ('a spirit doesn't have flesh and bones') and eat broiled fish. Luke's gathered disciples also include the Emmaus pair reporting the same day.

label: Jesus breathed on the disciples, said 'Receive the Holy Spirit', and gave authority to forgive or retain sins
statement: Jesus said 'Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you', breathed on them and said 'Receive the Holy Spirit! If you forgive anyone's sins, they have been forgiven them; if you retain anyone's sins, they have been retained' (20:21-23).
note: John's difference from Luke 24:49: Luke's Jesus commands the disciples to wait in Jerusalem until 'clothed with power from on high' (the Pentecost chronology of Acts 2), while John has the gift of the Spirit on Easter evening itself.

label: Thomas was absent at the first appearance and demanded to see and touch the nail prints and the side
statement: Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came; told 'We have seen the Lord!', he answered that unless he saw in Jesus's hands the print of the nails, put his finger into it and his hand into his side, he would not believe (20:24-25).
note: Thomas's absence and demand are John's detail alone among the Gospels.

label: Eight days later Thomas saw the risen Jesus and acclaimed 'My Lord and my God'
statement: After eight days the disciples were inside again with Thomas, the doors locked; Jesus came and stood in the middle, invited Thomas to reach his finger and hand into hands and side; Thomas answered 'My Lord and my God!', and Jesus pronounced blessed those who have not seen and yet believe (20:26-29).
note: Appearance claim, written and searched honestly; the eight-day interval and the confession are John's detail alone.

label: The evangelist names many other unwritten signs and states his purpose: that readers may believe
statement: Jesus did 'many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book; but these are written, that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in his name' (20:30-31) - the evangelist's own statement about the book's selection and aim.

label: The beloved disciple ('the disciple whom Jesus loved')
aka: traditionally identified with John son of Zebedee (disputed, not stated in the text)

label: First-century olive-tree and grapevine remains under the Church of the Holy Sepulchre
date: plant remains approximately 2,000 years old; excavation by Francesca Romana Stasolla reported 2025
method: archaeobotanical analysis (remnants, seeds and pollen) of soil samples extracted from beneath the stone floor of the church

label: Wikipedia: Church of the Holy Sepulchre (olive and grapevine remains, Stasolla excavation)
title: Wikipedia: Church of the Holy Sepulchre (olive and grapevine remains, Stasolla excavation)
excerpt: found remains of olive trees and grapevines that are approximately 2,000 years old. These plant remnants, seeds and pollen, were discovered via archaeobotanical analysis performed on soil samples that had been extracted from beneath the stone floor of the church.

label: Wikipedia: Disciple whom Jesus loved (identity disputed)
title: Disciple whom Jesus loved
excerpt: Since the end of the first century, the beloved disciple has often (but not unanimously) been identified with John the Evangelist.

label: The other disciple entered the tomb, saw and believed
statement: The other disciple, the one whom Jesus loved, entered the tomb, saw the linen cloths, and believed (20:8).
note: John alone has the beloved disciple's entry and belief; the Synoptics have no beloved disciple at the tomb. Reviewer 9: formerly asserted against claim:mt-28-06-resurrection, whose fact is Matthew's angelic announcement.
